# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 56 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 56 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_056_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

This chapter gives the first interpretation of the vineyard parable and is one of the most theologically complex passages in the Shepherd. The identification of the slave with the "holy spirit who dwelt in the flesh" (*to pneuma to hagion to katoikoun en tē sarki*) and the flesh as the servant is striking.

The question of *who* the slave represents is disputed. Three main interpretations: (1) The slave = Christ's human flesh; the son = the pre-existent divine Christ/Spirit; (2) The slave = the Holy Spirit in human flesh; (3) An adoptionist reading where the human Jesus earns divine status through his obedience. None of these maps cleanly onto later orthodoxy.

EMET uses "sacred spirit" for *to pneuma to hagion*; LOGOS and PNEUMA use "holy spirit." SOPHIA uses "Holy Spirit" — the standard English rendering.

The "first-created angels" (*hoi prōtoi ktisthentes*) in 56:4 are the angelic council of God's court — a standard early Jewish cosmological motif (1 Enoch 20; Rev 8:2).

---

## Similitude 5, Part 2 — First Interpretation of the Vineyard Parable

**56:1** I asked him to explain the parable to me. "What are you asking to understand?" he said. "Lord," I replied, "why was the son's inheritance not sufficient for the slave? Why was he established as co-heir with the son?"

**56:2** "Listen," he said. "The slave who kept the lord's commandment and instruction — he is the Holy Spirit who dwelt in the flesh. And his flesh served this Spirit well, walking in holiness and purity, not defiling the Spirit in any way."

**56:3** "When therefore this flesh had conducted itself so well and purely, and had labored together with the Spirit and cooperated with it in everything, conducting itself with valor and fortitude, he chose it as a partner with the Holy Spirit. For the conduct of this flesh pleased the Lord, in that it had not been defiled while bearing the Holy Spirit upon the earth."

**56:4** "He took the son and the trustworthy slaves as counselors. These are the holy angels who were created first. The master took counsel with them to the effect that this flesh — having served the Holy Spirit blamelessly — should have some resting place, lest it should appear to have lost the reward of its service."

**56:5** "For every flesh in which the Holy Spirit has dwelt shall receive a reward, if it is found undefiled and spotless. This, then, is the interpretation of this parable as well."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
